data.name: Carpus
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word κάρπος (karpos), meaning fruit, or fruitful. In the New Testament, Carpus is mentioned as one of the seven deacons appointed by the apostles to help with the distribution of food and other resources to the needy members of the early Christian community.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes growth and nourishment, both materially and spiritually.

in_hebrew.name: קרפוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קרפוס הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו רעים וחברים קרובים, והוא מוזכר בברית החדשה כאדם שהיה קרוב לפאולוס, השליח הנוצרי, והיה חלק מהקהילה הנוצרית הקדומה

in_greek.name: Κάρπος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Κάρπος είναι ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει φίλος και συγγενής, και αναφέρεται στη Καινή Διαθήκη ως πρόσωπο που ήταν κοντά στον Απόστολο Павλο και ήταν μέλος της πρώτης χριστιανικής κοινότητας

in_latin.name: Carpus
in_latin.long_meaning: Carpus est nomen Latinum quod significat amicum et proximum, et in Nova Testamenta mentionem habet ut persona quae erat propinqua Apostolo Paulo et erat pars primae communitatis Christianae

in_english.name: Carpus
in_english.long_meaning: Carpus is a name that means dear friend and close companion, and it is mentioned in the New Testament as a person who was close to the Apostle Paul and was part of the early Christian community

This name would have resonated with early Christians, who valued hard work, generosity, and selflessness.

The name also emphasizes the importance of being a good steward of the resources and blessings that have been given to us, and using them to make a difference in the lives of those around us.
